title: Does suppressing evaluation-awareness steering covertly increase misalignment?

original_idea.body: Test whether suppressing eval-awareness steering covertly increases misalignment by jointly measuring awareness and behavior. Inference-only, open model.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain to a critical pathway: eval-awareness and deceptive-alignment-adjacent behavior is recognized as important by major safety orgs (level 4).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires measuring misalignment with held-out probes and curated eval-awareness data; solid ML fundamentals needed (level 3).

narrow_scope.reasoning: Deliverable depends on building reliable awareness + misalignment measurement workstreams; multi-part (level 3).

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Neglected medium-horizon eval-awareness safety work, open models, weak lab incentive (level 4).

novelty.reasoning: Builds on an existing reproduction but characterizing the decoupling systematically may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Grounded in a prior reproduction; the systematic decoupling characterization may be open.
